title: Japan's Budget Restaurant Saizeriya Raises Prices
paragraphs: Saizeriya, a popular Italian restaurant chain in Japan, is famous for its very low prices. But now, even Saizeriya has decided to raise its prices.

On October 14, the company announced that prices at its restaurants in Japan would go up from October 29. On average, prices will rise by 6%. At 24 restaurants near leisure facilities and in some city areas, the increase will be bigger, at around 10% on average.
One of the chain's most famous dishes, Milano-style doria, will go up from 300 yen to 320 yen. Other dishes that currently cost 400 yen will rise to between 420 and 430 yen.

Saizeriya said it decided to raise prices because the cost of ingredients and energy has been going up. The company said it could no longer cover these rising costs on its own. In its announcement, the company also apologized to customers, saying its efforts had not been enough.

The price increase is a big change for Saizeriya and its loyal customers. According to reports, it is the first time the company has raised prices across its menu since it became a public company in 1998. For many years, Saizeriya was known as a place where people could eat a full meal for very little money, even while other restaurants were raising their prices.

Many people in Japan have been surprised by how customers reacted to the news. On social media, most people supported the price increase. Many said that Saizeriya's food had been too cheap for a long time and that a small increase of around 20 yen was completely fair.
The news shows how rising costs are affecting businesses in Japan. Even companies that work very hard to keep prices low are finding it difficult to avoid price increases.
